open_points.subject: A8 optional and required run settings
open_points.text: A required setting that is absent ends the start, and an optional one that is absent takes its default.
open_points.question: Does an environment variable that is present with an empty value count as absent, or as a supplied value that must be validated?
options: An empty value counts as absent for every setting.
An empty value is supplied and invalid for typed settings; string settings receive the empty string.
Empty handling is decided separately for each setting.
open_points.default_guess: Treat an empty value as absent, preserving the earlier startup behavior.

witness.initial: All required settings are valid and PORTAL_DELIVERER_PORT is present with the empty value.
outcomes: The empty value counts as absent, so port 8850 is used and the service can listen.
The empty value counts as a malformed supplied port, so the start ends without listening.
witness.observer: The deployment sees whether the service listens on port 8850.

open_points.subject: runtime setting value normalization
open_points.text: that module decides how a value is read
open_points.question: Before validation, are environment values used exactly as supplied, trimmed, case-normalized, or otherwise transformed?
options: Use every value exactly as supplied.
Trim ASCII whitespace from every value.
Apply setting-specific normalization, including possible case normalization for environment.
open_points.default_guess: Use values exactly as supplied; only the token file has an explicit trimming rule.

witness.initial: PORTAL_DELIVERER_TIMEZONE is set to ` Europe/Madrid ` and every other setting is valid.
outcomes: Whitespace is trimmed, Europe/Madrid is recognized, and startup continues.
The value is used literally, the time-zone database does not know it, and startup ends.
witness.observer: The deployment sees whether the service starts.

open_points.subject: PORTAL_DELIVERER_PORT representation
open_points.text: The port is a whole number from 1 to 65535
open_points.question: Which textual forms in the environment represent a whole-number port?
options: Only non-empty ASCII decimal digits are accepted.
A leading plus sign and leading zeroes are also accepted.
The runtime integer parser decides, including its handling of whitespace and non-ASCII digits.
open_points.default_guess: Accept only ASCII decimal digits, then require the parsed value to be from 1 through 65535.

witness.initial: PORTAL_DELIVERER_PORT is set to `+8850` and every other startup input is valid.
outcomes: `+8850` is accepted as the whole number 8850 and the service listens.
`+8850` has the wrong form and startup ends without listening.
witness.observer: The deployment sees whether the service listens.

open_points.subject: ownership of semantic run-setting rejection
open_points.text: A8 | reading each run setting, its default, and the refusal of a missing required setting or of a value of the wrong form | `runtime_settings` / A8 | the refusal of a well-formed port above 65535 and of a time zone the database does not know | `deliverer_service` / the refusal of a value the start-up table does not accept
open_points.question: Does runtime_settings or deliverer_service reject a well-formed but out-of-range port and a syntactically valid but unknown time zone?
options: runtime_settings rejects every value the start-up table does not accept.
runtime_settings rejects missing or syntactically malformed values, while deliverer_service rejects an out-of-range port and an unknown time zone.
deliverer_service performs all run-setting validation after runtime_settings reads raw values.
open_points.default_guess: Use the specific allocation: runtime_settings handles absence and form, while deliverer_service handles port range and time-zone existence.

witness.initial: PORTAL_DELIVERER_PORT is `70000`; all other environment values and files are valid.
events: If that call returns, capability:deliverer_service.run_service continues startup.
outcomes: load_runtime_settings rejects the value because the start-up table does not accept it.
load_runtime_settings returns a well-formed integer and deliverer_service rejects it later.
witness.observer: The startup caller and module-level tests see which capability fails.

open_points.subject: service_start validation step and failure precedence
open_points.text: capability:runtime_settings.load_runtime_settings reads the run settings from the environment. / capability:deliverer_service.load_config turns them into the context of the operations and calls capability:object_connections.load_connections once / capability:deliverer_service.run_service serves that surface in the web server, on the loopback interface and the `port` of the run settings.
open_points.question: Which named deliverer_service capability checks an out-of-range port and an unknown time zone, and where do those checks occur relative to loading the connections file and reading the token?
options: load_config validates both after load_connections but before read_token.
load_config validates the time zone, while run_service validates the port immediately before binding.
run_service validates both only after the application and token have been built.
open_points.default_guess: Have load_config validate both settings before it loads the connections file, so invalid startup configuration fails before installation files are read.

witness.initial: The port is 70000 and the connections file is invalid; the remaining startup inputs are valid.
events: Startup proceeds according to the chosen location of the port check.
outcomes: The port is rejected before capability:object_connections.load_connections is called.
load_connections runs first and the invalid connections file ends startup before the port is rejected.
witness.observer: A startup test or filesystem audit sees whether the connections file was read and which failure won.
